item.title: Tongan-American politician David Tangipa wins re-election to California State Assembly
item.description: Tongan-American politician David Tangipa has won re-election to the California State Assembly, securing a second term as a Republican representative for District 8 following the November 3 United States midterm elections. Tangipa, 30, first entered the state legislature in 2024 after defeating fellow Republican George Radanovich. He was unopposed on the ballot in this year’s general election.
item.content:encoded:
Tongan-American politician David Tangipa has won re-election to the California State Assembly, securing a second term as a Republican representative for District 8 following the November 3 United States midterm elections.

Tangipa, 30, first entered the state legislature in 2024 after defeating fellow Republican George Radanovich. He was unopposed on the ballot in this year’s general election.

His district covers parts of seven counties in central and eastern California, including Fresno, Madera, Mariposa, Calaveras, Inyo, Mono and Tuolumne.

Born in Sacramento on December 9, 1995, Tangipa is a first-generation Tongan-American whose mother is of Tongan descent. His father is a United States military veteran.

He attended California State University, Fresno, where he earned a bachelor’s degree in political science and criminology and later completed a Master of Business Administration.

Tangipa also played American football as a tight end for the Fresno State Bulldogs before pursuing a career in real estate.

Before entering the legislature, he worked for Fresno County Supervisor Nathan Magsig, gaining experience in local government.

During his first term, Tangipa served as vice-chair of the Assembly Budget Committee and held positions on several other legislative committees.

The California State Assembly is the lower chamber of the state’s legislature, responsible for passing state laws, approving budgets and overseeing government policies.

Its members serve two-year terms, unlike members of the United States Congress, who legislate at the federal level in Washington, DC.

Tangipa is among Tongan-Americans participating in elected public office in the United States, where established Tongan communities are concentrated in states including California, Utah and Hawaii.

Tangipa’s re-election comes as California remains home to one of the largest Tongan communities in the United States. According to US Census-based estimates for 2020–2024, approximately 27,779 people identifying as Tongan, either alone or in combination with another racial identity, live in California, with significant communities in San Mateo, Alameda, Santa Clara and Los Angeles counties.
